title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
why_read: A sharp empirical finding that most of the benefit from RL fine-tuning of image/video diffusion models can be replicated by a tiny constant steering vector, which is a meaningful simplification for anyone doing RL post-training.
analysis: The paper investigates what reinforcement learning fine-tuning actually changes inside diffusion transformer models used for image and video generation. Instead of learning complex, prompt-specific adjustments, the authors show that a single fixed set of steering vectors, added uniformly regardless of the input, can recover 90 percent or more of the reward gains from full RL fine-tuning while using 65 times fewer parameters. This suggests that much of what RL post-training does is a simple, input-independent push toward outputs the base model could already produce, not genuinely new input-dependent reasoning. That is a valuable and somewhat humbling insight for practitioners investing heavily in RL fine-tuning pipelines for generative models.
